title: license list
description: What <app> license list answers with -o json, on envelope/v2, for licenses of elderlygate/mankit/license/v2 (license-payload.schema.json): every license file the app can see, one row each, with the one active for this app marked, and every file it refused with why (ADR-L8). It is the one home of a license's fields: license show gives the active license, and license show <id> one license, in this answer's row (license.schema.json). mankit's license check makes it for every app, so every app answers it alike.

kind.description: Always LicenseList, the kind of this answer, so a reader knows which schema its data meets.

data.description: The licenses the app took and the files it refused.

licenses.description: Every license file the app read and took: the org licenses that name it and its own (ADR-L8), at most one of them active. The trial is not a license and is in license show's trial instead (ADR-L9). While mankit still reads mankit/v1's files, an org or product file shows as a license here (ADR-L8). A file it refused is in refused instead, never here. Empty when there is none, so a reader tells no license from a failure.

refused.description: Every license file the app read but did not take, so a refused file never shows as a license and a person sees why (ADR-L1, L5, L6, L8, L9). Its reason is one of signature, untrusted_key, other_build, unreadable, wrong_place, id_mismatch and retired_kind, each meaning what problem/v1's reason says. Empty when none was refused.

license.description: One license file the app read and took, a row of license list and the one shape license show gives a license in: its id and place, whom it names, what it opens or until when, the key that signed it, and whether it is the app's active one. Every one is of the payload's one kind, license (license-payload.schema.json), so it names no kind.

id.description: The license's id, as its signed payload says: the one a user names in license use <id> and license remove <id> (ADR-L8).

place.description: Where the license file sits (ADR-L8; the paths: the mankit README). org: the org's licenses folder, shared by every app; app: this app's own licenses folder. So a reader shows whose a license is, and license remove knows which file it removes.

for.description: Whom the license names, as its signed payload says.

lines.description: The product lines it opens, as its signed payload says, so a reader shows a license that never ends by what it opens. Absent when the payload names none.

issued.description: The license's first day, as its signed payload says, so a reader shows a license not begun yet.

until.description: The license's last day, as its signed payload says.

daysLeft.description: The days left until the license's last day, until, 0 once it has ended. Absent when the license never ends. license check gives only this; when to warn is the threshold's to say (ADR-L3).

ended.description: True once the license's last day, until, has passed: its features are locked again, and what they made stays readable (ADR-L3). Always false for a license that never ends.

active.description: True on the app's active license, the one its features and state rest on, and on at most one license (ADR-L8). It is the one license use or license add chose in this app; with no choice made, it is the newest license that names the app (ADR-L8); other apps keep their own choice. Still true when it has ended or does not name this build's line, as the app never switches to another license by itself. When the chosen file is refused, none here is true and license show's sentence says why.

allOf.description: An ended license has no days left.
A license meets its payload's rule: it either runs until a day or names the lines it opens, never both (license-payload.schema.json).
A license with a last day counts its days left to it; one that never ends has none and never ends.

refused.description: One license file the app read but did not take, and why, in the words of the Problem shape (ADR-S21), so a person sees why and license remove <id> can name it.

id.description: The name license remove <id> takes for the file: for a file in a licenses folder, its file name less .license, as <id>.license names it (ADR-L8), never the file's own metadata.id, which is not signed and which a junk file could fake. For an old single license file it is that metadata.id, as the file has no name to give one. Absent for a file that gives none, such as an old single file too broken to read an id from, which license remove cannot name.

window.description: The countdown the License group's bar shows, present only while one shows: a running trial (ADR-L9), or a license in the warning the threshold of ADR-L3 sets. Its days left are daysLeft beside it.

of.description: The countdown's whole length in days: ADR-L9's trial length, or the warning window mankit reads from the threshold (ADR-L3), so the bar shows daysLeft out of it.
